entries.meaning: I ceaselessly bow to the worshipful Rāma, lord of Jānakī and foremost of Raghu's line, mounted upon Puṣpaka: blue as a peacock's throat and bearing the radiant mark of a foremost Brahmin's lotus foot, resplendent in yellow cloth, lotus-eyed and ever gracious, holding arrow and bow, accompanied by the monkey host and served by his brother.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review. The tightly compounded vipra-pādābja-cihnam is rendered as the auspicious foot-mark borne by Viṣṇu-Rāma.

words: bearing the radiant mark of a foremost Brahmin's lotus foot
I bow to the worshipful one
the foremost of Raghu's line, ceaselessly

entries.meaning: The two lovely lotus feet of the lord of Kosala are tender and revered by Brahmā and Maheśa, caressed by Jānakī's lotus hands, and companions of the bee that is the contemplative devotee's mind.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

words: the two lovely lotus feet of the lord of Kosala
the two tender feet revered by Brahmā and Maheśa
the two caressed by Jānakī's lotus hands
companions of the bee that is the mind

entries.meaning: I bow to Śaṅkara, liberator from Kāma: fair and lovely as jasmine, moon and conch; husband of Ambikā and giver of the desired attainment; compassionate and beautiful lotus-eyed.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review. Anaṅga-mocanam is read as liberation from Kāma, with ‘destroyer of Kāma’ remaining a contextual alternative.

words: fair and lovely as jasmine, moon and conch
husband of Ambikā and giver of the desired attainment

entries.meaning: One day remained of the appointed term, and the people of the city were deeply distressed. Everywhere women and men worried, their bodies grown thin through separation from Rāma.
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: Every omen became favourable and everyone's mind grew joyful, as though announcing the Lord's arrival; the city was lovely on every side.
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: The minds of all the mothers, beginning with Kausalyā, felt such joy—as though someone now wished to say, ‘The Lord has arrived together with Sītā and his younger brother.’
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: Bharata's eye and right arm throbbed again and again. Recognising the omen, his mind rejoiced greatly and he began to reflect.
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.
